breakfast.name: Sadza (Maize Porridge)
instructions: Boil water
Stir in mealie meal gradually
Cook until very thick and pulls from pot
breakfast.description: Thick maize porridge — Zimbabwe's staple, eaten three times daily.

breakfast.name: Maputi (Popcorn)
instructions: Pop corn in hot oil
Season with salt
breakfast.description: Popcorn — a common Zimbabwean breakfast or snack.

breakfast.name: Bota (Thin Porridge)
instructions: Bota is the thin Zimbabwean porridge -- the lighter breakfast version of sadza
Maize meal cooked to a thin, drinkable consistency (unlike thick sadza)
Sweetened with sugar or enriched with peanut butter
The morning version: thin and sweet. The main meal version (sadza): thick and unsweetened
Given to children and the elderly -- easy to eat and nutritious
Drunk from a cup or eaten with a spoon
breakfast.description: Zimbabwean thin porridge -- bota, maize meal cooked to a drinkable consistency (unlike thick sadza). Sweetened with sugar or enriched with peanut butter. Given to children and the elderly. The lighter breakfast version of the national staple.

breakfast.name: Dovi with Bread (Peanut Butter Porridge)
instructions: Dovi (peanut butter) porridge is a Zimbabwean breakfast -- peanut butter cooked into a creamy porridge
Peanut butter dissolved in hot water or milk to create a thick, nutty porridge
Or simply: peanut butter on bread with tea
Dovi (peanut butter) is central to Zimbabwean cuisine -- used in cooking and as a spread
Zimbabwe produces excellent groundnuts -- the peanut butter is often homemade
The simplest Zimbabwean breakfast: thick bread with peanut butter and sweet tea
breakfast.description: Zimbabwean peanut butter breakfast -- dovi, peanut butter dissolved into hot porridge or spread thick on bread with sweet tea. Zimbabwe produces excellent groundnuts. Dovi is central to the cuisine -- used in cooking and as a spread. Often homemade.

breakfast.name: Fried Eggs with Tomato and Onion
instructions: Fried eggs with tomato and onion -- the Zimbabwean quick breakfast
Eggs fried in oil with a simple tomato-onion sauce
Served with bread or sadza
A protein-rich breakfast for those who can afford eggs
The tomato-onion combination is the base of most Zimbabwean cooking
Quick and simple -- made in every Zimbabwean kitchen
breakfast.description: Zimbabwean quick breakfast -- fried eggs with tomato and onion sauce. Served with bread. The tomato-onion combination is the base of most Zimbabwean cooking. Quick, simple, protein-rich.

lunch.name: Sadza ne Nyama (Porridge with Meat)
ingredients: Beef stew: beef, tomatoes, onion, garlic, salt
instructions: Make thick sadza
Make beef stew
Serve sadza with stew on the side
Eat by hand — pinch sadza, dip in stew
lunch.description: Sadza with beef stew — the Zimbabwean national meal.

lunch.name: Muriwo une Dovi (Greens in Peanut Sauce)
instructions: Cook greens until tender
Make peanut sauce with tomatoes and onion
Combine
Serve with sadza
lunch.description: Greens in peanut butter sauce — the essential sadza relish.

lunch.name: Sadza ne Muriwo (Porridge with Greens)
ingredients: Muriwo: collard greens, rape (canola leaves), or pumpkin leaves
instructions: Sadza ne muriwo is the most basic and most common Zimbabwean meal
Sadza: the thick maize porridge that is the heart of every Zimbabwean meal
Muriwo: cooked leafy greens (the vegetable relish)
The greens are cooked with tomato and onion -- sometimes with groundnut powder for richness
Eaten with the right hand: a ball of sadza is formed, an indentation pressed with the thumb, used to scoop muriwo
This meal is eaten daily by the majority of Zimbabweans -- it IS the national diet
Sadza without muriwo is considered incomplete -- the relish provides the nutrition and flavor
lunch.description: The most common Zimbabwean meal -- sadza ne muriwo, thick maize porridge with cooked leafy greens in tomato-onion sauce. Eaten with the right hand: sadza ball formed, thumb pressed, used to scoop muriwo. Eaten daily by the majority. Sadza without muriwo is incomplete.

lunch.name: Road Runner Chicken
ingredients: Free-range chicken (road runner -- indigenous breed, small and lean)
instructions: Road runner chicken is the Zimbabwean free-range chicken -- smaller, leaner, and tastier than broilers
Called "road runner" because indigenous chickens roam freely -- running across roads
Tougher than commercial chicken but much more flavorful
Cooked slowly in a tomato-curry sauce until tender
Curry powder: introduced during the colonial era, now a Zimbabwean pantry staple
Road runner chicken is prized -- it costs more than commercial chicken at the market
Served with sadza -- the chicken sauce is the relish
lunch.description: Zimbabwean free-range chicken -- road runner, indigenous breed that roams freely (running across roads). Smaller, leaner, tougher, but much more flavorful than broilers. Slow-cooked in tomato-curry sauce. Prized and costs more than commercial chicken. Served with sadza.

lunch.name: Matemba (Dried Kapenta)
ingredients: Dried kapenta (matemba -- small dried fish from Lake Kariba)
instructions: Matemba is the Zimbabwean name for dried kapenta fish -- the same fish as in Zambia
Lake Kariba straddles the Zimbabwe-Zambia border -- both countries harvest kapenta
Sun-dried and sold in markets across Zimbabwe
Cooked with tomato, onion, and sometimes groundnut powder
An affordable protein source for millions of Zimbabweans
The tiny fish are eaten whole -- bones, heads, and all
lunch.description: Zimbabwean dried fish -- matemba (kapenta from Lake Kariba, shared with Zambia). Sun-dried tiny fish cooked with tomato, onion, and groundnut powder. Eaten whole. An affordable protein source for millions. Lake Kariba straddles the Zimbabwe-Zambia border.

lunch.name: Nyama Choma (Grilled Meat)
instructions: Nyama choma is grilled meat -- the East and Southern African braai/barbecue tradition
Meat grilled over charcoal -- simply seasoned with salt
Beef is most common in Zimbabwe (cattle are culturally and economically important)
Served with sadza, coleslaw, and chili sauce
A social event -- nyama choma is eaten at gatherings, beer halls, and celebrations
The Shona and Ndebele cattle traditions: cattle are wealth, status, and food
lunch.description: Zimbabwean grilled meat -- nyama choma, beef or goat on charcoal with salt. A social event at gatherings, beer halls, and celebrations. Served with sadza and coleslaw. Shona and Ndebele cattle traditions: cattle are wealth, status, and food.

lunch.name: Derere (Okra Stew)
instructions: Derere is the Zimbabwean okra stew -- okra cooked until it releases its characteristic slime
The mucilaginous texture of okra is appreciated in Zimbabwean cooking -- not avoided
In Western cooking, okra slime is often seen as undesirable; in Zimbabwe, it provides a silky sauce
Cooked with tomato and onion, sometimes with peanut butter for richness
A common vegetable relish (ndiwo) served with sadza
Okra is widely grown in Zimbabwean home gardens
lunch.description: Zimbabwean okra stew -- derere, okra cooked until it releases its characteristic slime (appreciated as a silky sauce, not avoided). With tomato, onion, and sometimes peanut butter. A common vegetable ndiwo with sadza. Widely grown in home gardens.

dinner.name: Madora (Mopane Worms)
instructions: Soak and wash dried worms
Fry with onion and tomatoes
Add peanut butter for richness
Serve with sadza
dinner.description: Fried mopane worms in peanut sauce — high-protein traditional food.

dinner.name: Mazondo (Cow Trotters)
instructions: Boil trotters 3 hours until gelatinous and tender
Season with onion, garlic, tomatoes, chili
Serve with sadza
dinner.description: Slow-cooked cow trotters — rich and gelatinous.

dinner.name: Dovi (Peanut Butter Chicken Stew)
ingredients: Peanut butter (dovi -- smooth, homemade or commercial)
instructions: Dovi is the Zimbabwean peanut butter stew -- the signature flavor of Shona cuisine
Chicken cooked in a rich peanut butter sauce with tomato and onion
The peanut butter dissolves into the sauce creating a thick, creamy, nutty gravy
Sometimes greens are added for nutrition and color
Dovi (peanut butter) is the most important flavoring in Zimbabwean cooking
The dish is named after the ingredient: dovi IS peanut butter in Shona
Served over sadza -- the peanut sauce soaks into the porridge
Comfort food -- the taste of home for every Zimbabwean abroad
dinner.description: Zimbabwean signature dish -- dovi, chicken stewed in rich peanut butter sauce with tomato and onion. Dovi means peanut butter in Shona. The most important flavoring in Zimbabwean cooking. The peanut butter creates a thick, creamy, nutty gravy. The taste of home for every Zimbabwean abroad.

dinner.name: Muboora (Pumpkin Leaf Stew)
instructions: Muboora is the Zimbabwean pumpkin leaf stew -- cooking the leaves of the pumpkin plant
Young pumpkin leaves cooked with peanut butter, tomato, and onion
The peanut butter creates the rich sauce that coats the leaves
In Zimbabwe, pumpkin leaves are a more common vegetable than the pumpkin itself
Grown in home gardens and communal plots -- free and abundant in season
A nutritious, affordable relish -- green vegetables with protein from peanut butter
dinner.description: Zimbabwean pumpkin leaf stew -- muboora, young leaves cooked in peanut butter sauce. In Zimbabwe, pumpkin LEAVES are more commonly eaten than the pumpkin itself. Grown in home gardens and communal plots. Nutritious and affordable -- greens with peanut butter protein.

dinner.name: Huku ne Sadza (Chicken Stew with Sadza)
instructions: Huku ne sadza is Zimbabwean chicken stew with sadza -- the celebration meal
Chicken cooked in a tomato-curry sauce
When a guest arrives at a Zimbabwean home, a chicken is often slaughtered for them -- the highest honor
The Shona saying: "You don't cook a chicken when you hear the visitor approaching -- you do it when they arrive"
Curry powder is widely used in Zimbabwean cooking -- a colonial-era addition that became essential
Served with sadza -- the chicken sauce is the main relish
dinner.description: Zimbabwean celebration meal -- huku ne sadza, chicken in tomato-curry sauce. When a guest arrives, a chicken is slaughtered -- the highest honor. Shona saying: you don't cook it when you hear the visitor -- you do it when they arrive. Curry powder: colonial-era addition, now essential.

dinner.name: Biltong Stew
instructions: Biltong stew uses dried cured beef (biltong) rehydrated and cooked into a stew
Biltong: beef cured with salt, vinegar, and coriander, then air-dried -- Southern African tradition
Different from jerky: biltong is air-dried (not smoked or dehydrated), thicker, and more flavorful
The biltong rehydrates in the tomato sauce as it cooks
A way to use biltong that has hardened too much to eat as a snack
Biltong-making is a Zimbabwean tradition -- many families make their own
dinner.description: Zimbabwean dried meat stew -- biltong (air-dried cured beef, Southern African tradition -- NOT jerky) rehydrated in tomato-onion sauce. Different from jerky: air-dried, thicker, more flavorful. A way to use biltong too hard for snacking. Many families make their own biltong.

snacks.name: Chimodho (Corn Bread)
instructions: Mix all ingredients
Pour into pan
Bake at 175°C 30 min
snacks.description: Sweet corn bread with peanut butter.

snacks.name: Magwinya (Fat Cakes)
instructions: Magwinya are Zimbabwean fat cakes -- deep-fried dough balls
A yeast dough shaped into balls and deep-fried until golden and puffed
The same concept as South African vetkoek or Zambian vitumbuwa
Sold at markets, schools, and roadside stands -- a cheap snack
Eaten plain, with jam, or with mince (ground beef filling)
The school-gate snack: children buy magwinya after school
A filling, affordable snack when times are tight
snacks.description: Zimbabwean fat cakes -- magwinya, yeast dough deep-fried into golden puffed balls. Like South African vetkoek. Sold at markets, schools, and roadside stands. The school-gate snack. Affordable and filling. Eaten plain, with jam, or with mince.

snacks.name: Boiled Groundnuts
instructions: Boiled groundnuts -- peanuts boiled in salted water until soft
Different from roasted groundnuts: boiled peanuts are soft, starchy, and savory
Sold in small bags at markets and bus stations
The peanut shell softens enough to open easily
A cheap, protein-rich snack
Boiled groundnuts are a Southern African tradition (also popular in the American South)
snacks.description: Zimbabwean boiled peanuts -- groundnuts boiled in salted water until soft and starchy (different from crunchy roasted). Sold at markets and bus stations. Also a tradition in the American South. Cheap, protein-rich snack.

snacks.name: Roasted Maize (Chibage)
instructions: Chibage is Zimbabwean roasted maize on the cob -- the seasonal street food
Fresh green maize roasted on charcoal until the kernels char and caramelize
Available during the maize harvest season (February-May)
Sold at roadsides and markets by women with small charcoal braziers
The smell of roasting maize signals the harvest season has arrived
Eaten off the cob, with salt if desired
snacks.description: Zimbabwean seasonal street food -- chibage, fresh green maize cobs roasted on charcoal until kernels char and caramelize. Available during harvest (February-May). Sold by women with charcoal braziers. The smell signals harvest season has arrived.

snacks.name: Biltong
instructions: Biltong is the Zimbabwean and Southern African air-dried cured beef -- the national snack
Lean beef cured in salt, vinegar, and coriander, then hung to air-dry for 3-7 days
Different from jerky: biltong is air-dried (not heat-dried), thicker, and retains more flavor
The coriander seeds are the defining spice -- crushed and pressed into the meat surface
Sliced thin or torn into strips and eaten as a high-protein snack
Every butchery and supermarket in Zimbabwe sells biltong
Making biltong at home is a Zimbabwean tradition -- families have their own recipes and biltong boxes
Droewors: the dried sausage version -- thin sausage air-dried like biltong
snacks.description: Southern African air-dried cured beef -- biltong, lean beef cured in salt, vinegar, and crushed coriander, hung to air-dry 3-7 days. NOT jerky (air-dried, not heat-dried, thicker, more flavorful). Every butchery sells it. Families have their own recipes and biltong boxes. The national snack.

desserts.name: Nhopi (Pumpkin Mash)
instructions: Boil pumpkin until tender
Mash with peanut butter and sugar
desserts.description: Sweet pumpkin mash with peanut butter.

desserts.name: Maheu Ice Lollies
instructions: Maheu ice lollies -- frozen maheu sold as popsicles
Maheu (the fermented maize drink) frozen in small plastic bags
Sold by vendors from cooler boxes -- a cheap frozen treat
Slightly sour and sweet -- the fermented flavor is unique
A creative way to sell maheu in hot weather
The Zimbabwean equivalent of freeze pops
desserts.description: Zimbabwean frozen treat -- maheu ice lollies, fermented maize drink frozen in plastic bags. Sold from cooler boxes. Slightly sour and sweet. The Zimbabwean equivalent of freeze pops. Creative way to sell maheu in hot weather.

desserts.name: Sweet Potato Balls
instructions: Sweet potato balls -- mashed sweet potato shaped into balls, rolled in sugar, and fried
A simple dessert using abundant sweet potatoes
The natural sweetness of the potato with added sugar and cinnamon
Fried until golden and slightly crispy on the outside
Made at home as a treat -- simple ingredients, simple technique
desserts.description: Zimbabwean sweet potato balls -- boiled sweet potato mashed, shaped, and fried with sugar and cinnamon. Simple home dessert using abundant sweet potatoes. Golden and slightly crispy outside, soft inside.

desserts.name: Doughnut (Zimbabwean Style)
instructions: Zimbabwean doughnuts -- yeast-raised, deep-fried, and rolled in sugar-cinnamon
Sold at bakeries and by street vendors
Not ring-shaped -- usually round balls or oblongs
The bakery tradition in Zimbabwe reflects British colonial influence
A treat and a celebration food -- bought for birthdays and gatherings
Hot from the fryer, coated in sugar -- simple and beloved
desserts.description: Zimbabwean yeast doughnuts -- round balls deep-fried and rolled in sugar-cinnamon. Sold at bakeries and by street vendors. British colonial baking influence. A celebration food bought for birthdays and gatherings.

desserts.name: Chikenduza (Fried Dough Twists)
instructions: Chikenduza are Zimbabwean twisted fried dough -- twisted strips of sweet dough deep-fried
Dough twisted into rope-like shapes and fried until golden
Coated in sugar after frying
Similar to South African koeksisters but without the syrup dip
A market sweet and home treat
The twist shape gives maximum crispy surface area
desserts.description: Zimbabwean fried dough twists -- chikenduza, sweet dough twisted into rope shapes and deep-fried golden, coated in sugar. Similar to South African koeksisters but without the syrup dip. Maximum crispy surface area from the twist shape.

drinks.name: Maheu (Fermented Maize Drink)
instructions: Cook thin porridge
Cool, add malt
Ferment 1-2 days
Serve cold
drinks.description: Tangy fermented maize drink — Zimbabwe's refreshment.

drinks.name: Seven Days (Traditional Beer)
instructions: Cook maize porridge
Add sprouted rapoko
Ferment 7 days
Strain and serve
drinks.description: Traditional millet beer — fermented for seven days.

drinks.name: Mazoe Orange Crush
ingredients: Mazoe Orange Crush concentrate (Zimbabwean brand since 1906)
instructions: Mazoe Orange Crush is Zimbabwe's national drink -- a concentrated orange squash
Produced in Mazoe, Mashonaland Central -- since 1906
A concentrated syrup diluted with water -- not juice, not soda
Every Zimbabwean household has a bottle of Mazoe
Mazoe IS Zimbabwe -- it is the national drink the way Coca-Cola is American
Multiple flavors now: orange, blackberry, lemon, peach -- but the original orange is iconic
Served at every Zimbabwean gathering, party, and funeral
For Zimbabweans abroad, Mazoe is the taste of home -- it's shipped internationally to the diaspora
drinks.description: Zimbabwe's national drink since 1906 -- Mazoe Orange Crush, concentrated orange squash diluted with water. Every household has a bottle. Mazoe IS Zimbabwe. Multiple flavors but original orange is iconic. For the diaspora, Mazoe is the taste of home -- shipped internationally.

drinks.name: Rock Shandy
instructions: Rock Shandy is the Zimbabwean and Southern African non-alcoholic mixed drink
Lemonade and soda water mixed with a few dashes of Angostura bitters
The bitters give it a slightly herbal, aromatic complexity
A "fancy" non-alcoholic drink -- served at braais and social gatherings
Popular across Southern Africa: Zimbabwe, South Africa, Botswana
The British colonial legacy: bitters and lemonade drinks
drinks.description: Southern African non-alcoholic drink -- Rock Shandy, sparkling lemonade and soda water with dashes of Angostura bitters. The bitters add herbal, aromatic complexity. Served at braais and social gatherings. British colonial legacy across Zimbabwe, South Africa, and Botswana.
